# Personalized Shopping Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Personalized Shopping Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 6 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm licensing for your tenant and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved retail environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available and keep the workshop Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded shopping knowledge, the proposed preference and catalog feeds, and channel limits; document blocked paths instead of bypassing them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the consented preference feed and the read-only product and inventory feed, with least-privilege references; the synthetic workshop needs none. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare personal-shopper, clienteling, retail-manager and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: the Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Consent and preference ownership | Have the business owner confirm which preference fields shoppers explicitly provide and how opt-in is recorded before real profiles replace the synthetic ones. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Retail business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Styling preparation, preference lookup and availability checks per appointment, as done today Establish how consistent styling preparation is today before attributing change to the adapted agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Appointment or request | Preference source | Opt-in recorded | Options prepared | Availability check method | Associate reviewer | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Retail business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Retail business owner | Approve preference and catalog sources, shopper-facing scope and success measures; keep every order, benefit and stock decision with authorized associates. |
| Authorized associates | Review draft recommendations and outfits and verify inventory in the live system before any customer commitment. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm tenant licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any shopper connection is approved. |
| Preference and commerce connection owners | Approve the consented preference feed and read-only product and inventory feed; record each connection identity and least-privilege reference. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check PSA-01 through PSA-04, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject evidence lacking its markers or Draft state. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route shopper decisions to authorized associates. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures are agreed before production.
- [ ] The business owner records how styling preparation, preference lookup and availability checks work today before agreeing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/personalized-shopping-assistant/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and approved publisher prefix are recorded before any build lane starts.
- [ ] The authentication option, required sign-in and allowed audience are approved for shopper preferences and inventory data.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/personalized-shopping-assistant/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/personalized-shopping-assistant/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/personalized-shopping-assistant/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/personalized-shopping-assistant/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Personalized Shopping Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_shopping-assistant-rules-and-safety.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_shopping-assistant-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: inventory-check
9. Add skill: outfit-builder
10. Add skill: product-recommendations
11. Add skill: style-profile
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass PSA-01: Personal Shopper
15. Pass PSA-02: Clienteling Specialist
16. Pass PSA-03: Retail Manager
17. Pass PSA-04: Personal Shopper
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: PSA-01, PSA-02, PSA-03, PSA-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If Easy mode is chosen, the source-controlled project uses cli-copilot in the approved environment and stays Draft.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `PersonalizedShoppingAssistantAgent` and returns `Draft Product Recommendations`.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged locked prompt passes in its own fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Case passes rest on the deterministic validator; an annotated image is a learner checkpoint, not the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing shopper preferences or inventory data. Request only the scopes needed for approved preference and catalog sources. Restrict the allowed audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Approved consented preference feed

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Preference and commerce connection owners

1. **Bind Approved consented preference feed — read:** Bind consent-scoped read-only connector or API actions.

2. **Identity for Approved consented preference feed:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved consented preference feed:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved consented preference feed:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Decline the inference; repeat only the stated preferences. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim live availability, a reservation or an order.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved read-only product and inventory feed

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Preference and commerce connection owners

1. **Bind Approved read-only product and inventory feed — read:** Bind read-only catalog and inventory actions; keep reservations in a separate approved workflow.

2. **Identity for Approved read-only product and inventory feed:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved read-only product and inventory feed:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved read-only product and inventory feed:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Make no availability promise; the synthetic snapshot needs live-system verification. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim live availability, a reservation or an order.

### Step 3-3. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Preference and commerce connection owners

Bind only approved read-only preference and catalog connections; keep reservations, orders and benefits out of the agent.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved connections preserve the reviewed input and output contract; no live lookup, reservation or order is claimed without tool evidence.
- [ ] Only approved read-only connections are bound, and any write action stays separate.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as intended associates and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user connection access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic match scores, stock counts and totals are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations identify the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked shopping corpus | All four cases, PSA-01 through PSA-04, return every required marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Privacy and transaction boundary | Any sensitive inference, reservation, benefit, order, return, refund or purchase is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a visible positive anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required captures. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Retail business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Retail business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved associate audience and supported channels are configured and tested before publication.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review shopping session transcripts, failed interactions, connection errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
